meta.title: Awesome Jev
meta.subtitle: A field guide to typed decision systems

thesis.headline: State in. Typed decisions out.
thesis.body: Jev is trending because it turns high-frequency bounded choices into a typed probability surface. The ecosystem around that primitive is young, fast, and already splitting into applications, infrastructure, and open research.

timeline.title: Jev launches in early access
timeline.detail: System One and RLCD become public concepts.

timeline.title: NanoJev artifacts appear
timeline.detail: Small-model experimentation expands beyond API wrappers.

timeline.title: Framework integrations arrive
timeline.detail: Spring AI and related adapters lower the switching cost.

timeline.title: Ollaya breaks out
timeline.detail: A local runtime makes the wire shape portable.

timeline.title: Snapshot for this atlas
timeline.detail: The ecosystem is still measured in weeks, not years.

recommendations.title: Hosted trial
recommendations.body: Use the official SDK plus the System One adapter. Gate on confidence and measure your own workload.

recommendations.title: Local trial
recommendations.body: Use Ollaya to compare open decision models behind a familiar protocol. Treat it as emerging infrastructure.

recommendations.title: Research
recommendations.body: Use NanoJev, jevlike, or JEV-27B to study distinct open strategies rather than one supposed reproduction.
